To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the biomass production of S. spallanza nii is higher in eutrophic than in oligotrophic areas and (2) the polychaetes can be co-reared with mussels on long lines with low mortality, high increase in biomass and volume, low cost, and a high profit.

the polychaetes Sabella spallanazanii reared on suspended plastic nets in the Mediterranean Sea grow producing a biomass higher and faster than the natural population and that this biomass can be coupled to mussel farming in a non-fed system with a low environmental impact and a high profit.

Sabella spallanza-nii is an interesting species to be cultured in a mussel farm because it can produce high-value biomass with no additional food supply and with no environmental impact, and that the technology to culture Sabella spallan-zanii in a mussel long-line farm is feasible and can be applied to medium-sized farms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of rearing Sabella spallananzanii in eutrophic areas of the Mediterranean Sea, with a low cost of production, and a high profit.
the development of a new aquaculture technique for producing a high-value marine product in a eutrophic environment, where the environmental impact is reduced, and the production costs are low.
the development of a technology to obtain high-quality polychaetes in a sustainable way, with the aim of improving the economic sustainability of the Mediterranean aquaculture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrated the possibility to produce high-value polychaete biomass, coupled with mussel biomass, in a completely nonfed culturing system without any impact on the environment.

the present study demonstrates the possibility to obtain a high-value polychaete biomass coupled to mussels in a completely non fed culturing system without environmental impacts due to mussel rearing.
this work is the first to show that Sabella spallanazani is a good candidate for the production of high-value biomass in a eutrophic coastal area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polychaetes can be reared with low cost in eutrophic areas and that the rearing of S. spallanza nii is a good alternative to the rearing of the mussel M. galloprovinci a l in the same areas.

the co-cultivation of Sabella spallanazanii with Mytilus in the Mar Picollo of Taranto, in a eutrophic environment, is a promising way to obtain a high-value product, with low costs and low environmental impact, in a sustainable way.

the polychaetes reared in a eutrophic environment, as the Mar Piccolo, can produce a biomass that is 10 times higher than that of natural populations, thus representing a good candidate for the aquaculture of the Mediterranean Sea.

the polychaetes reared in euritic conditions can produce biomass with a value of 2.3 €/kg (wet weight) that can be sold at a price higher than that of the mussels (1.2 €/kg) reared in the same farm.
the polychaetes Sabella spallanizanii can be successfully reared in euryhaline conditions, in the presence of suspended plastic nets, and in a co-culture system with mussels.
the polychaetes can be reared in a pilot plant with a low production cost and high profit.
